_note: Sowing/harvest windows and nutrient doses are general Indian recommendations (ICAR / state package-of-practice ranges). Always confirm against a local soil-health card.

crops.name: Rice (Paddy)
crops.tip: Keep 2–5 cm standing water during tillering; drain 10 days before harvest.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.tip: The crown-root stage (21 days) is the most critical irrigation.

crops.name: Maize
crops.tip: Do not let it dry at tasselling and silking — that is where yield is made or lost.

crops.name: Cotton
crops.tip: Scout for pink bollworm from squaring; use pheromone traps early.

crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.tip: Earthing up at 90–120 days prevents lodging.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.tip: Treat seed with rhizobium; it fixes its own nitrogen, so do not overdose urea.

crops.name: Groundnut
crops.tip: Gypsum at pegging improves pod filling.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.tip: Stake the plants and remove lower leaves to slow early blight.

crops.name: Onion
crops.tip: Stop irrigation 2–3 weeks before harvest so bulbs cure well.

crops.name: Potato
crops.tip: Earth up twice; exposed tubers turn green and become unsellable.

crops.name: Chilli
crops.tip: Watch for thrips causing leaf curl in dry spells.

crops.name: Sunflower
crops.tip: Hand-pollinate or keep bee boxes near the field to improve seed set.

crops.name: Ragi (Finger millet)
crops.tip: A dependable dryland crop; line sowing beats broadcasting on yield.

crops.name: Jowar (Sorghum)
crops.tip: Thin to one plant per 10–12 cm; crowding cuts grain size.

crops.name: Tur (Pigeon pea)
crops.tip: Nip the tips at 45 days to encourage branching and more pods.

crops.name: Gram (Chana)
crops.tip: One light irrigation at pod filling lifts yield noticeably.
